target_customer: Software, developer tool and infrastructure companies (plus some larger enterprises) that want AI assistants and coding agents to find, cite and correctly use their product
problem: Buyers increasingly ask ChatGPT and other AI tools which product to use, and products that AI systems do not know or cannot operate lose discovery and signups. Companies lack tooling to see how AI describes them and to make docs and workflows usable by agents.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services: AI visibility audits, a monitoring and content hosting platform, and an agent experience testing product
product_category: Generative engine optimization and agent experience

founders.name: Kevin Chandra
previous_startups: Cotter (passwordless auth SDK, acquired by Stytch)
founders.background_notes: Repeat YC founder with two earlier exits per the YC page and TechCrunch.

founders.name: Albert Purnama
founders.background_notes: Some outlets spell the surname Punama.

technical_complexity.rationale: Core work is prompt monitoring across AI engines, generating and hosting machine readable pages, and agent task testing. A small team with prior SDK and website builder experience could build the first version quickly, though keeping up with changing AI engine behavior is ongoing work.

defensibility.rationale: Methods are easy to copy and many tools entered the category within months. Early enterprise logos and hosted page footprint (TechCrunch cited about half a million pages for one Fortune 10 customer) give some switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: SEO suites pushed back by adding AI search features, and dedicated GEO players raised large rounds during 2025 and 2026. No acquisition of the company has been reported.

market_need_then: In 2025 AI assistants became a discovery channel and the founders told TechCrunch most growth on websites was coming from AI bots rather than people. Brands wanted to know whether ChatGPT mentioned them, which created fast demand for visibility tooling.

branding.domain_note: Uses promptingcompany.com, which includes the word The in the brand but not in the domain.

identity.visual_style: Minimal and technical, abstract textures with bracketed step markers such as STEP 01
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct short declarative lines such as optimize for Agent Experience

branding.brand_signature: The term Agent Experience as a category phrase
branding.community_and_virality: A TBPN interview in September 2025 and TechCrunch seed coverage in October 2025 gave the company press, but no evidence found of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Plain descriptive name with some founder driven press, but no mascot, community or distinctive identity found in sources.

outcome_analysis: The company is a young repeat founder team that rode the 2025 shift toward AI search and raised a 6.5 million dollar seed about four months after starting, with named software customers. No shutdown, sale or layoffs were found, so the outcome is still open. Its main risk is a crowded category where better funded rivals and SEO suites compete on the same visibility metrics.
notes: Competitor list left empty because every competitor source found was dated 2026 or undated, and none is dated near the Summer 2025 batch; named later players in outcome terms include Profound, Peec AI, AthenaHQ, Otterly and Scrunch AI. A Salestools report lists a 25M valuation and StartupHub lists 13M raised; both are single source and unverified. A profile mentions a June 2026 company announcement naming Standard Capital and Kearny Jackson, which could not be verified and may reflect a later round. The lead investor varies by outlet. The YC standard investment is not recorded as a round. Founder education was not found.
